method.label: Bound the sides using the altitude

annotationRationale: The triangle area formula determines the altitude, and the shortest-perpendicular property forces a perimeter strictly greater than 50.
sourceMethod: Follows the official alternative solution using the altitude and side-length bounds. Names the perpendicular foot and explains why at least one side exceeds 20.

review.mathCheck: The area forces altitude 20. Each remaining side is at least 20, and both cannot equal 20 because their perpendicular feet would require A=B. Thus the perimeter exceeds 50 for every position of C, giving 0 points, choice A.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful, originally worded adaptation of the alternative MAA AMC 10B solution 10, page 5. The introduced perpendicular foot explains the official side bounds and strict inequality without requiring the ellipse approach.
review.annotationCheck: Both assessed nodes match the proof. Taking the foot on the entire line handles exterior altitudes and either side of AB; the equality cases are explicitly resolved.
